seo.answer_capsule: VIP Home Painting is the luxury house painting company serving Irvine, CA and all six of its villages — Orchard Hills, Altair, Portola Springs, Hidden Canyon, Woodbury and Stonegate. We repaint exteriors, interiors and kitchen cabinets using Sherwin-Williams Emerald and Duration coatings applied with professional Graco and Titan airless equipment. Every project begins with a complimentary 30-minute consultation in which our design team renders your actual home in each candidate palette. Exterior work starts at $4.75 per square foot of paintable surface, itemized line by line, backed by a 2-Year Warranty. Call (909) 312-5400.
seo.viz_intro: Irvine is not one place with one light. Orchard Hills sits against the ridge where afternoon sun pushes warm colors yellow by two. Woodbury’s garden paseos stay filtered and cool. Hidden Canyon takes canyon mornings and hot open afternoons in the same day. The same white behaves like three different colors across those villages, which is why a fan deck decided indoors tells you almost nothing. Choose a direction below and watch a real home change, then let our design team do it with the front of your house.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to paint a house in Irvine?
faqs.a: VIP exterior work in Irvine starts at $4.75 per square foot of paintable surface — the premium end of the local range, which runs roughly $2.74 to $4.89. Every estimate is itemized line by line: prep, primer, coating, trim and accents priced separately, never a lump sum. Paintable surface is the actual area being coated, which is not the same as your home’s square footage. Call (909) 312-5400 for a walkthrough and an itemized figure.

faqs.q: Which Irvine villages do you serve?
faqs.a: All of them. We have dedicated pages for Orchard Hills, Altair, Portola Springs, Hidden Canyon, Woodbury and Stonegate, and we work throughout the rest of Irvine as well. Each village has its own architecture, light conditions and design-review process, so the palette guidance genuinely differs between them.

faqs.q: How do your prices compare to other Irvine contractors?
faqs.a: We are usually more expensive, and we say so plainly. Most painters in this market publish no pricing at all. The difference is in preparation, Sherwin-Williams Emerald and Duration rather than builder-grade product, and seeing the color on your own home before anything is committed. A repaint done twice costs the whole amount again, which is what makes getting it right the first time the cheaper path.

faqs.q: Do you repaint ceilings and interiors, or only exteriors?
faqs.a: Both. Interiors cover walls, ceilings, trim and crown molding, with full masking and daily clean-up. We also refinish kitchen cabinets — doors and drawers sprayed off-site in urethane enamel, boxes sprayed in place, hardware re-hung square, which produces a factory finish rather than a painted one.

faqs.q: How long does an exterior repaint take in Irvine?
faqs.a: Most Irvine exteriors are completed in three to five working days, sequenced one side at a time so the house stays livable throughout. Larger estates with extensive trim, stone detailing or a full color change take longer. Your schedule is agreed in writing before the crew arrives.

faqs.q: What paint do you use, and why does it matter here?
faqs.a: Sherwin-Williams Emerald and Duration exterior systems, applied at the full thickness the manufacturer specifies and never over-thinned. Inland Irvine sun is hard on coatings: builder-grade paint chalks and fades years early, and deep colors in particular fail fast without fade-resistant colorants. All work carries a 2-Year Warranty on labor and materials.

faqs.q: Do you handle HOA and design review approval?
faqs.a: Yes, as part of the project. Nearly every Irvine village requires approval before an exterior color change. We assemble the submission package — swatches, Sherwin-Williams product data sheets and a callout for each side of the house — formatted for your association’s review. We also paint common areas for associations directly; see our HOA and common-area page.

We render the actual buildings in every scheme under consideration, so the vote happens on something residents can see rather than something they have to imagine. faqs.q: Do you work with Irvine HOA management companies?

faqs.q: What common areas do you paint for associations?
faqs.a: Clubhouse interiors and exteriors, pool houses and cabanas, perimeter walls, community monuments, guard houses and gate structures, park shelters, mailbox kiosks, trash enclosures, and wrought iron fencing and railings. If it is association-maintained and it takes paint, it is in scope.

faqs.q: How do you price common-area painting?
faqs.a: Itemized by structure rather than as a single lump figure, so your board can compare our proposal against others line by line and approve scope selectively if the budget requires phasing. faqs.q: Can the board see the colors before approving them?

faqs.q: What insurance and documentation do you provide?

All supplied with the proposal, not after the award.

faqs.q: Will the work disrupt residents or close amenities?
faqs.a: We sequence building by building so amenities stay open wherever possible, and agree work hours and resident-notice lead times with management before anyone arrives on site. Crews are briefed on gate and pool-area protocol, landscaping and hardscape are protected, and the site is left clean every evening.

flashback.h2: Years in the Same Color: The 3 Reasons an Irvine Repaint Gets Put Off
flashback.lead: Irvine is not one place with one light. Orchard Hills takes the late sun off the ridge, Woodbury’s paseos stay filtered and cool, and Hidden Canyon swings from canyon shade to open glare in a single day. A color that behaves in one village can misbehave a mile away, and that is where the waiting starts.
body: For years, {their} house wore the color it had when they moved in. Not because they loved it. Because every time the subject came up, three things stopped them.

The first was the chip: a two-inch square under store light that said nothing about a whole house in afternoon sun. The second was the street, because whatever they chose, the neighbors would live with too. The third was the bill. A repaint that turned out wrong would cost the whole job a second time.

So nothing changed, and the house kept wearing a color nobody had chosen. In Irvine the same three reasons come with one more: a design review that wants the decision in writing before a crew is booked, which gives the wait another reason to go on.

instead.h2: Palette Books, Sample Patches, Asking Around: 5 Things That Never Showed an Irvine House Whole
instead.bridge: {They} did what careful owners do. Before anything was rendered, they worked through the list below — every step reasonable, and not one of them able to show the whole house in its own light.
instead.lede: In Irvine the list usually starts with the association’s palette book. It narrows the choice to colors the village will accept, and says nothing about how any of them will look across your walls at four in the afternoon. Then come the sample pots: a square on the garage, another by the front door, each one right at the hour you happen to check it. Neighbors are asked. The finalists are compared side by side on a card, and each loses to an undertone nobody saw coming.
instead.turn: Nobody in that story did anything wrong. A palette book and a sample square are the tools the industry hands you, and neither can show a whole Irvine house in the light it actually stands in.
